groups.title: game
groups.text: The game tree, Instances, players, creatures and outlines.

groups.title: Characters
groups.text: game.Me for your own character, its signals, and the fields of every character.

groups.title: Stats
groups.text: The numbers the game keeps for a character, and the modifiers that are on it.

groups.title: Items
groups.text: game.Items, inventories and what a character carries.

groups.title: Session
groups.text: game.Time, game.Weather, game.Prospect and the players of the session.

groups.title: Creatures
groups.text: The fields of a creature, spawning one, and what the tables of the game say about a kind.

groups.title: Models
groups.text: What game.Creatures:GetModel gives for the 3D model control.

groups.title: Tables
groups.text: game.Data: the tables of the game, read as plain Lua and changed for as long as a mod is loaded.

groups.title: Recipes
groups.text: game.Recipes: finding crafting recipes and changing what they take, give and where they are made.

groups.title: Store
groups.text: game.Workshop: the store on the station, its categories, nodes and prices.

groups.title: Assets
groups.text: game.Assets: assets of the game by path, materials of your own and shapes made of numbers.

groups.title: Blueprints
groups.text: game.Blueprints: things described in Lua and spawned, and their parts.

groups.title: Animations
groups.text: game.Animations: clips of the game and animations written as keys, on characters, creatures and things.

groups.title: Effects
groups.text: game.Effects and game.Sounds: particles, lights, trails, shakes and sounds.

groups.title: ui
groups.text: The menu, windows, overlays, notifications, tags, hotkeys and themes.

groups.title: Controls
groups.text: What goes in a window: text, buttons, switches, sliders, lists and grids.

groups.title: task
groups.text: Run code alongside the game: wait, delay and repeat.

groups.title: Signal
groups.text: Events, the functions connected to them, and game.Frame for every frame.

groups.title: storage
groups.text: Keep values when the mod reloads and when the game restarts.

groups.title: mod
groups.text: What a mod knows about itself, require, and the functions that are blocked.

groups.title: log
groups.text: Write to the Wax log.

types.name: WaxWindowOptions
types.title: WaxWindowOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Window takes.

props.name: title
props.text: "Window" when omitted.

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name shown before the title. The menu's Icons page lists the names.

props.name: width
props.text: Default 340, or 520 with side navigation.

props.name: height
props.text: Default 420, or 380 with pages.

props.name: closable
props.text: False leaves out the close button.

props.name: resizable
props.text: False makes a window the player cannot resize: it has no grip, its edges and corners do nothing, and it is always the size your mod gives it. SetSize still works.

props.name: visible
props.text: False creates the window hidden.

props.name: nav
props.text: Gives the window pages, listed down the side or along the top.

props.name: nav_width
props.text: Width of the side navigation column.

props.name: remember
props.text: False stops Wax remembering the window's position and size between sessions.

props.name: pinned
props.text: True keeps the window on the screen while the player plays, with the menu closed. It takes no clicks then, so the mouse stays with the game. With a menu open it is a window like any other.

props.name: key
props.text: The key that shows and hides your mod's windows, such as "F6" or "Ctrl+K". The first window a mod makes decides. Without it Wax gives the mod a key, and the player can choose another on the mod's card of the Mods page.

types.name: WaxPageOptions
types.title: WaxPageOptions
types.text: The options that window:Page takes.

props.name: icon
props.text: Icon name shown before the page's name. The menu's Icons page lists the names.
props.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, { icon = "text" })

props.text: Lists the page at the bottom of a side navigation column.

types.name: WaxPage
types.title: WaxPage
types.text: A page of a window that has navigation. It is a container for controls.
types.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)

signals.name: PressedAgain
signals.text: Fires when the page's own name is pressed while the page is already showing. Use it to go back to the start of a page that has several views.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)
page.PressedAgain:Connect(function()
    print("PressedAgain")
end)

signals.name: NearEnd
signals.text: Fires while the end of the page is in view: when the user scrolls close to the bottom, and a few times a second while the page is not full. Add more content in the handler, or do nothing when there is no more.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)
page.NearEnd:Connect(function()
    print("NearEnd")
end)

types.name: WaxWindow
types.title: WaxWindow
types.text: A window in the menu. Controls added to it go into its body, or into a first page called "Main" when it has pages. The player moves it by its title bar and resizes it by any edge or corner; the bottom right corner shows a grip. Resizing stops at the window's minimum size and at the edges of the screen. A mod's windows come up together, with that mod's key (see ui.Keys), and other mods' windows stay as they are.
types.use: local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })

signals.name: Opened
signals.text: Fires when the window is shown.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.Opened:Connect(function()
    print("Opened")
end)

signals.name: Closed
signals.text: Fires when the window is hidden.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.Closed:Connect(function()
    print("Closed")
end)

signals.name: PageChanged
signals.text: Fires with the name of the page that was selected.
signals.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window.PageChanged:Connect(function(name)
    print(name)
end)

funcs.name: SetTitle
funcs.text: Changes the text in the title bar.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetTitle(title)

funcs.name: SetPosition
funcs.text: Moves the window, keeping it on the screen.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetPosition(x, y)

funcs.name: SetSize
funcs.text: Resizes the window, no smaller than its minimum size.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetSize(width, height)

funcs.name: SetNavWidth
funcs.text: Sets the width of the navigation column of a window made with nav = "side".
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetNavWidth(width)

funcs.name: Show
funcs.text: Shows the window, in front of the others. While the menu is open it comes up at once, with your mod's other windows. While the menu is closed it waits for your mod's key or for ui.Open().
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:Show()

funcs.name: Hide
funcs.text: Hides the window. Hiding the last window that is up closes the menu.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:Hide()

funcs.name: SetVisible
funcs.text: Shows or hides the window.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetVisible(shown)

funcs.name: IsVisible
funcs.text: True while the window is shown. A shown window is on screen only while its mod's windows are up: IsShowing tells you that.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local result = window:IsVisible()

funcs.name: IsShowing
funcs.text: True while the window is really on screen: it is shown, and its mod's windows are up (or every window is, in preview).
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local result = window:IsShowing()

funcs.name: SetMinimized
funcs.text: Minimises the window to its title bar, or restores it.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SetMinimized(minimized)

funcs.name: IsMinimized
funcs.text: True while the window is minimised.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local result = window:IsMinimized()

funcs.name: StatusBar
funcs.text: Adds a status line along the bottom of the window, or returns the one the window already has. `text` sets its message.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local statusBar = window:StatusBar(text)

funcs.name: Destroy
funcs.text: Removes the window and everything on it.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:Destroy()

funcs.name: Page
funcs.text: Adds a page to a window made with nav = "side" or "top". The first page added is selected.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
local page = window:Page(name, options)

funcs.name: RemovePage
funcs.text: Removes a page made with Page, with everything on it.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:RemovePage(page)

funcs.name: SelectPage
funcs.text: Switches to the page with this name.
funcs.use:
local window = ui.Window({ title = "Example" })
window:SelectPage(name)

types.name: WaxOverlayOptions
types.title: WaxOverlayOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Overlay takes.

props.name: anchor
props.text: Where on the screen the panel is pinned. "top-right" when omitted.

props.name: x
props.text: Distance in from the anchor's edge. Default 16.

props.name: y
props.text: Distance in from the anchor's edge. Default 16.

props.name: width
props.text: Default 240.

props.name: title
props.text: Adds a heading.

props.name: background
props.text: False leaves out the panel behind the controls.

props.name: movable
props.text: False stops the player dragging it while the menu is open. Where it was dragged to is remembered.

types.name: WaxOverlay
types.title: WaxOverlay
types.text: A panel pinned to the screen that stays up during play and never takes the mouse.

types.name: WaxPanelOptions
types.title: WaxPanelOptions
types.text: The options that ui.Panel takes.

props.name: when
props.text: When it shows: "cursor" (the default) while the Wax menu is open or one of the game's own screens has the mouse, "menu" only with the Wax menu, "always" whenever it is switched on.

props.name: padding
props.text: Space between its edge and its controls.

props.name: height
props.text: A fixed height. As tall as its controls when omitted.

props.name: zoom
props.text: Draws everything in it this much larger (1.25 is a quarter larger). Text stays sharp.

props.name: opacity
props.text: How solid its background is, 0 to 1. 0.96 when omitted.

props.name: visible
props.text: False makes it hidden until SetVisible(true).

props.name: on_press
props.text: Runs when the panel is pressed where it has no control.
props.use: local overlay = ui.Panel({ on_press = function() end })

props.name: place
props.text: Where the panel goes on a screen of this size. It is asked when the panel is made and again, in the same frame, whenever the game's window changes size: the panel that exists is moved, sized and zoomed, and nothing is built again. The size is the real screen in the units the game lays its own menus out in, and the zoom is used as it is, so such a panel keeps its size beside the game's menus whatever the interface size is.
props.use: local overlay = ui.Panel({ place = function(screen_width, screen_height) end })

types.name: WaxPanelPlace
types.title: WaxPanelPlace
types.text: What a panel's place function answers. What is left out stays as it is.

types.name: WaxFitOptions
types.title: WaxFitOptions
types.text: The options that ui.FitGame takes.

props.name: scale
props.text: How large the game's menus are drawn, 0.5 to 1. 0.85 when omitted.

props.name: corner
props.text: The corner they shrink towards. "bottom-left" when omitted, which frees the right and the top.

props.name: x
props.text: Moves them sideways after they are made smaller, as a share of the screen. Right is positive.

props.name: y
props.text: Moves them up or down after they are made smaller, as a share of the screen. Down is positive.

props.name: enabled
props.text: False makes the request wait for SetEnabled(true).

types.name: WaxFit
types.title: WaxFit
types.text: A request to draw the game's own menus smaller.
types.use: local fit = ui.FitGame(options)

funcs.name: Set

params.name: x
params.text: Keeps its value when omitted.

params.name: y
params.text: Keeps its value when omitted.

funcs.text: Changes how large the game's menus are drawn, and how far they are moved when x or y is given. The numbers mean what the `scale`, `x` and `y` options mean.
funcs.use:
local fit = ui.FitGame(options)
fit:Set(scale, x, y)

funcs.name: SetEnabled
funcs.text: Switches the request on or off. While it is off the game's menus have their own size, unless another request is on.
funcs.use:
local fit = ui.FitGame(options)
fit:SetEnabled(on)

funcs.name: Remove
funcs.text: Gives the game's menus their own size back.
funcs.use:
local fit = ui.FitGame(options)
fit:Remove()

props.name: name

props.name: open

types.name: WaxKeys
types.title: ui.Keys
types.text: The keys that show and hide windows. Wax's own panel has one, and so has every mod that made a window: a key shows and hides its owner's windows and nobody else's. A mod's key is the one the player chose on the mod's card of the Mods page, else the one the mod asked for with ui.Window({ key = "F6" }), else a key Wax gives it once and remembers: one that no window and no hotkey of any mod uses. A press that your mod's own ui.Hotkey takes is not also taken as the key of its windows.

signals.name: Changed
signals.text: Fires with the owner and its new key when a key is changed.

funcs.name: Get
funcs.text: The key of an owner: "Wax" or a mod's id. Left out, it is the mod that asks.
funcs.use: local result = ui.Keys.Get(owner)

funcs.name: Set

params.name: owner
params.text: "Wax" or a mod's id.

params.name: key
params.text: An engine key name such as "F6". It can be held with Ctrl, Shift or Alt: "Ctrl+K".

funcs.text: Gives an owner another key, or none with nil. A key that another owner has, or that another mod uses as a hotkey, is refused: the key stays what it was, a notification says who has it, and you get false and that name.
funcs.use: local changed, taken_by = ui.Keys.Set(owner, key)

funcs.name: Owners

types.name: WaxUI
types.title: ui
types.text: The GUI library: the menu (windows you click), overlays (panels you only read) and notifications.

props.name: Icons
props.text: Icon names: the bundled Lucide set ("shield", "wrench", "map-pin" ...) plus images that mods register.

props.name: Notifications
props.text: What all notifications share: the corner they show in and how many show at once. It also counts them and closes them all.

props.name: Debug
props.text: The in-game debug panel.

props.name: Pictures
props.text: The game's own pictures, such as item icons, which a cell of a Slots control shows by their path. Loading them is given a few milliseconds a frame, so a picture can show a moment after it was asked for.

props.name: Keys
props.text: The keys that show and hide windows. Wax's own panel has one, and so has every mod that made a window: a key shows and hides its owner's windows and nobody else's. A mod's key is the one the player chose on the mod's card of the Mods page, else the one the mod asked for with ui.Window({ key = "F6" }), else a key Wax gives it once and remembers: one that no window and no hotkey of any mod uses. A press that your mod's own ui.Hotkey takes is not also taken as the key of its windows.

signals.name: Opened
signals.text: Fires when the menu opens: somebody's windows come up and the mouse is freed.

signals.name: Closed
signals.text: Fires when the menu closes: nobody's windows are up any more and the game has the mouse back. A mod that opened the menu with `windows = false` also hears it when its own ui.Close() leaves the menu open for others.

signals.name: KeyChanged
signals.text: Fires with the new key of Wax's own panel. For any owner's key, use ui.Keys.Changed.

signals.name: ThemeChanged
signals.text: Fires with the theme's name after SetTheme or ResetTheme.

signals.name: ScreenChanged
signals.text: Fires once with the new size when ScreenSize gives another answer: after the game's window or the interface size has stopped changing for a moment, never while it is still being resized.

signals.name: GameScreenChanged
signals.text: Fires with what GameScreen answers, in the frame the game shows another of its menu screens, another tab of its main menu, or none any more (nil). Connect to it in place of asking GameScreen every frame: the game is only looked at while somebody listens.

funcs.name: Open

params.name: options
params.text: `windows = false` frees the mouse for panels only and brings no window up.

funcs.text: Shows your mod's windows and frees the mouse to use them. Other mods' windows and the Wax panel stay as they are. In the command bar it is the Wax panel that comes up.

funcs.name: Close
funcs.text: Hides your mod's windows again. The menu closes, and the game has the mouse back, once nobody's windows are up.
funcs.use: ui.Close()

funcs.name: Toggle
funcs.text: Shows your mod's windows when they are away, and hides them when they are up.
funcs.use: ui.Toggle()

funcs.name: Copy
funcs.text: Puts text on the clipboard, for pasting anywhere.
funcs.use: ui.Copy(text)

funcs.name: TextWidth
funcs.text: How wide a line of text is drawn, in the units controls and panels are sized in. It is worked out from the letters, to within a few percent.
funcs.use: local width = ui.TextWidth(text, options)

funcs.name: Shorten

returns.name: cut
returns.text: True when the text did not fit.

funcs.text: The text if it fits in a width, else its start with "..." after it. A little room is kept spare, as the library does for its own text.
funcs.use: local shown, cut = ui.Shorten(text, width, options)

funcs.text: True while the menu is open: the mouse is free, because somebody's windows are up.
funcs.use: local result = ui.IsOpen()

funcs.name: SetPreview
funcs.text: Shows every window without taking the mouse (for screenshots and for looking while you play).
funcs.use: ui.SetPreview(on)

funcs.text: True while the windows are shown in preview.
funcs.use: local result = ui.IsPreview()

funcs.name: SetToggleKey
funcs.text: Sets the key that shows and hides Wax's own panel, by the engine's key name ("F8"). nil leaves the panel without a key. A key that somebody has is refused, as with ui.Keys.Set. Every mod has a key of its own: see ui.Keys.
funcs.use: local changed, taken_by = ui.SetToggleKey(key)

funcs.name: GetToggleKey
funcs.text: The key that shows and hides Wax's own panel.
funcs.use: local result = ui.GetToggleKey()

funcs.name: Window
funcs.text: Creates a window in the menu. It is removed again when the mod reloads.
funcs.use: local window = ui.Window(options)

funcs.name: Overlay
funcs.text: Creates a panel pinned to the screen that stays up during play and lets clicks through.
funcs.use: local overlay = ui.Overlay(options)

funcs.name: Panel
funcs.text: Creates a panel whose controls take the mouse. It has no title bar and shows beside the game's own screens.
funcs.use: local overlay = ui.Panel(options)

funcs.name: Hovered
funcs.text: The value of the slot under the mouse, then its look and its Slots control. Nothing when no slot is under it.
funcs.use: local value, look, control = ui.Hovered()

funcs.name: IsTyping
funcs.text: True while a text box of Wax has the keyboard.
funcs.use: local result = ui.IsTyping()

funcs.name: ScreenSize
funcs.text: The size of the screen in the units windows and panels are laid out in. It changes with the shape of the game's window and with the interface size. While the game is starting and has no screen yet, the answer is 1920 by 1080; ScreenChanged fires if the real one turns out different.
funcs.use: local width, height = ui.ScreenSize()

funcs.name: FitGame
funcs.text: Draws the game's own menus (inventory, crafting, benches) smaller, which leaves room beside them for panels. They keep working as before. The request ends when the mod reloads.
funcs.use: local fit = ui.FitGame(options)

funcs.name: GameScreen
funcs.text: The game's own menu screen that is showing now: "UMG_MainMenu", "UMG_EscapeMenu", or a bench or container such as "UMG_Processor_C". For the main menu the second value is its tab: 0 inventory, 1 crafting, 2 tech tree, 3 talents, 4 map. Nothing when none shows.
funcs.use: local name, tab = ui.GameScreen()

funcs.name: Tag

params.name: target
params.type: WaxInstance|{ X: number, Y: number, Z: number }

funcs.text: Puts a line of text over an actor, over one part of an actor, or on a spot in the world. It follows what it is on, shows through walls, and tags that would cover each other pile up. The tag goes away by itself when the actor does.
funcs.use: local tag = ui.Tag(target, options)

funcs.name: Notify
funcs.text: Shows a short message in a corner of the screen. Sending the same message again restarts the one already showing.
funcs.use: local notification = ui.Notify(text, options)

funcs.name: Windows
funcs.text: A list of every window.
funcs.use: local windows = ui.Windows()

funcs.name: Hotkey

params.name: key
params.text: An engine key name such as "F6", "K" or "MiddleMouseButton" (a Keybind control gives you these). It can be held with Ctrl, Shift or Alt: "Ctrl+Three", "Ctrl+Shift+K".

funcs.text: Runs `callback` when the key is pressed during play. The hotkey is removed when the mod reloads.
funcs.use: local hotkey = ui.Hotkey(key, function() end, options)

funcs.name: IsKeyDown

params.name: key
params.text: An engine key name such as "A", "LeftShift" or "MiddleMouseButton".

funcs.text: True while the key is held down, as the game's own input reports it for the local player. It takes the key names ui.Hotkey takes. A name with Ctrl, Shift or Alt ("Ctrl+K") is true only while the key is down with exactly those held; a plain name is true whatever else is held. It is false while the game has no local player, and for a name the game does not know. It does not look at whether the menu is open or a text box has the keyboard (see ui.IsTyping). Every call asks the game, so use it in a loop that runs while something is held, such as one a ui.Hotkey started, and not in every frame of the game. It raises an error for a key that is not text, for empty text, and for a word before the key that is not Ctrl, Shift or Alt.
funcs.use: local result = ui.IsKeyDown(key)

funcs.name: MinScale
funcs.text: The smallest interface size that still draws text at a readable size on this screen. It follows the size of the game's window.
funcs.use: local result = ui.MinScale()

funcs.name: SetScale
funcs.text: Sets the interface size, where 1 is normal. The size is kept between ui.MinScale() and 2, and the size applied is returned.
funcs.use: local applied = ui.SetScale(scale)

funcs.name: GetScale
funcs.text: The interface size in use.
funcs.use: local result = ui.GetScale()

funcs.name: SetTheme
funcs.text: Switches to a named theme, or changes single settings from a table. Everything on screen takes the new colours in place, so no window is rebuilt and no mod is reloaded. Sizes and shapes apply to what is built afterwards.
funcs.use: ui.SetTheme(theme)

funcs.name: ResetTheme
funcs.text: Puts every theme setting back to the "Midnight" defaults.
funcs.use: ui.ResetTheme()

funcs.name: Themes
funcs.text: The names of the built-in themes, then of the ones added with AddTheme.
funcs.use: local list = ui.Themes()

funcs.name: AddTheme
funcs.text: Adds a theme: a table with any of the colour settings (window, panel, raised, text, accent ...) as "#RRGGBB".
funcs.use: ui.AddTheme(name, colors)

funcs.name: ThemeName
funcs.text: The name of the theme in use.
funcs.use: local result = ui.ThemeName()

funcs.name: Color
funcs.text: Makes a colour from "#RRGGBB" or 0xRRGGBB, with an optional alpha of 0..1.
funcs.use: local color = ui.Color(hex, alpha)

funcs.name: Theme
funcs.text: The table of the theme in use. Its colours follow the theme, so pass them as they are (color = ui.Theme().accent).
funcs.use: local theme = ui.Theme()

funcs.name: AddSettings
funcs.text: Adds Wax's own settings (the key of its panel, theme, accent, animation, size) to a container, such as a "Settings" page.
funcs.use: ui.AddSettings(container)

funcs.name: GetPropertyChangedSignal
funcs.text: A signal for one value of the object: a property of the game's that holds a number, true or false, text or an object, or a field Wax gives the class. It fires with (value, previous) when the value is found changed. The value is read ten times a second, and only while a handler is connected. An object arrives as an Instance, or nil when the property holds none. A table a field returns is compared by what it holds. `seconds` sets another time between reads, up to 3600. It is rounded to the nearest 0.05, and anything under 0.05 counts as 0.05. When one value is asked for at two paces, the faster is used. It works on an actor in the world and on a component that a property of its actor holds. Anything else raises an error that says why. When the object is gone, reading stops and every handler is disconnected. A task that waits on the signal is then not woken. A wrong name raises an error that suggests the right one.

local signal = instance:GetPropertyChangedSignal(name, seconds)

funcs.text: Puts a new wild creature into the world with the game's own spawn. kind is a variant such as "Conifer_Wolf" or "Deer", or a kind that has one variant. When it is omitted the creature goes six metres in front of your character, and the options may stand in its place. Wax asks the game for ground a creature can walk on near the place, within 5 metres to the sides and at any height, and puts the creature a little above it. Where the game has none it raises an error and nothing is spawned. Inside a task Spawn waits until the game has given the creature its level, two seconds at most, and then answers the creature. Outside a task it answers at once, and Level and Health are right a few frames later. It answers nil and the reason when the creature left the world before it was finished. A tamed variant is refused in this version of Wax. The game's call took 3 to 4 ms when it was timed, and 18 ms once: a kind that is not in memory is loaded by the game inside the call. What is spawned stays when the mod unloads, unless the option keep is false.

When it is omitted the mount comes a few metres in front of you, and the options may stand in its place. Where the game knows no ground to walk on under the place, as on a platform a mod built, the mount is made on the ground below and brought up. Inside a task it answers once the saddle is on, with the reason as a second value when the saddle did not go on. Outside a task it answers at once and finishes a moment later. props.text: Where it is, in the engine's units: 100 is one metre. Assign a place to move it there at once: { X = 0, Y = 0, Z = 0 }, { 0, 0, 0 }, an actor or game.Me. When the game finds no room there it raises an error that says so.

props.type: { X: number, Y: number, Z: number }?
props.text: How fast it moves along each axis, in the engine's units a second.

props.name: Swimming

signals.name: Damaged
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(who: WaxCharacter, amount: integer, info: WaxDamageInfo)>
signals.receives: who: WaxCharacter, amount: integer, info: WaxDamageInfo
signals.text: Fires when the game says this character took damage: the character, the damage of the hit, and what the game knows of it. The game tells it itself, so nothing is looked at meanwhile, and the handler runs in the same frame or the next one. Health that goes down with no hit, as when a mod assigns Health, is not damage. Seen on the host of a session. On another player's machine it has not been tried.
signals.use:
local character = game.Character
character.Damaged:Connect(function(who, amount, info)
    print(who, amount, info)
end)

signals.name: Died
signals.text: Fires once when this character is dead. After a hit that left it no health that is the frame of the hit or a moment later, and info says what did it. A death with no hit is seen by looking four times a second while a handler is connected, and info is empty then. A character that lives again and dies again is told again. When the character leaves the world, the handlers of its Damaged and Died are disconnected.
signals.use:
local character = game.Character
character.Died:Connect(function(who, info)
    print(who, info)
end)

params.type: WaxInstance|WaxMe|{ X: number, Y: number, Z: number }

types.name: WaxPlayerCharacter
types.title: WaxPlayerCharacter
types.text: What Wax adds to a player's character, on top of what every character has: every Instance whose class is IcarusPlayerCharacter or is built on it. Food, Water and Oxygen can be assigned as well.
types.use: local character = game.Character

props.name: Food
props.text: How much food it has left. It can be assigned: the number is rounded and brought between 0 and MaxFood.

props.name: MaxFood
props.text: The most food it can have.

props.name: Water
props.text: How much water it has left. It can be assigned: the number is rounded and brought between 0 and MaxWater.

props.name: MaxWater
props.text: The most water it can have.

props.name: Oxygen
props.text: How much oxygen it has left. It can be assigned: the number is rounded and brought between 0 and MaxOxygen.

props.name: MaxOxygen
props.text: The most oxygen it can have.

props.name: Radiation
props.text: Its radiation level.

props.name: MaxRadiation
props.text: The highest its radiation level goes.

props.name: BodyTemperature
props.text: The temperature of its body, in degrees Celsius.

props.name: Weight
props.text: What it carries in all its inventories, in kilograms. The game works it out a moment after the items change, not in the same frame.

props.name: MaxWeight
props.text: The weight it can carry, in kilograms: the game's stat WeightCapacity_+.

props.name: PlayerName
props.text: The name of the player who controls it. nil while the game has not said.

props.name: CharacterName
props.text: The name the player gave this character, such as the one on the character screen. nil while the game has not said.

props.name: Local
props.text: True for the character this player controls.

props.name: InCave
props.text: True while the game counts it as inside a cave.

types.name: WaxMe
types.title: game.Me
types.text: The local player's character, whichever one that is. game.Me is not an Instance: it finds the character each time it is used, so it goes on working after a respawn and on another map. It has every field and function of the character, and Character, Exists and the signals listed here. While there is no character, as at the title screen, Exists is false, a field reads nil, and calling a function or assigning a field raises an error that says so. A signal is fed by looking at the character a few times a second, and only while a handler is connected to it. What changes and changes back between two looks is not seen. A signal that hands over a value and the one before does not fire while there is no character, and for it another character whose value is not the last one seen counts as a change. Damaged and the three item signals are not fed by looking: the game tells Wax itself, through a hook on the game's own function that is made when the first handler connects. A handler never runs inside the game's call: what was heard is told from the frame loop, in the same frame or the next. All of it was seen on the host of a session. As a guest in someone else's game it has not been tried.

props.name: Character
props.text: The character itself, as an Instance. nil while there is none.

props.name: Exists
props.text: True while the local player has a character.

signals.name: HealthChanged
signals.text: Fires when health is not what it was at the last look. Looked at ten times a second.

signals.name: StaminaChanged
signals.text: Fires when stamina is not what it was at the last look. Looked at ten times a second.

signals.name: FoodChanged
signals.text: Fires when food is not what it was at the last look. The game says when it changed it, and that is looked at in the same frame or the next. Besides that it is looked at every two seconds, or twice a second where the game's word cannot be listened to.

signals.name: WaterChanged
signals.text: Fires when water is not what it was at the last look. Told and looked at as FoodChanged is.

signals.name: OxygenChanged
signals.text: Fires when oxygen is not what it was at the last look. Told and looked at as FoodChanged is.

signals.name: WeightChanged
signals.text: Fires when the weight carried, in kilograms, is not what it was at the last look. The game says when it worked a new weight out, a moment after the items changed, and that is looked at in the same frame or the next. Besides that it is looked at every two seconds, or twice a second where the game's word cannot be listened to.

signals.name: Damaged
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(who: IcarusPlayerCharacter, amount: integer, info: WaxDamageInfo)>
signals.receives: who: IcarusPlayerCharacter, amount: integer, info: WaxDamageInfo
signals.text: Fires when the game says your character took damage, as Damaged of a character does. It stays connected through a respawn and a map change. With damage told, HealthChanged follows in the same frame instead of at its next look.

signals.name: Died
signals.text: Fires once when your character is dead: in the frame of the hit that ended it, with what did it, or at the look that tells of a respawn (four times a second) when no hit came with the death.

signals.name: ModifierAdded
signals.text: Fires for a modifier that is on your character and was not at the last look. Looked at twice a second. The record has no Remaining: ask GetModifiers for what counts down. The modifiers a character has when it becomes yours are where it starts from, not something added.

signals.name: ModifierRemoved
signals.text: Fires for a modifier that was on your character at the last look and is not any more, with the record as it was. Looked at twice a second.

signals.name: ItemAdded
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?)>
signals.receives: item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?
signals.text: Fires when your character carries more of an item than a frame before, over all its inventories: the item's name as the game spells it, how many more, and a stack it went onto, with its Inventory. The game tells of every slot it changes. What moves from one slot or inventory to another within a frame is not added and not removed.

signals.name: ItemRemoved
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?)>
signals.receives: item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?
signals.text: Fires when your character carries fewer of an item than a frame before: the item, how many fewer, and a stack it came out of as that was before.

signals.name: ItemChanged
signals.text: Fires for every slot of what your character carries that holds something else than a frame before: what it holds now, nil for nothing, and what it held, each with its Inventory. A tool that wore and a stack that moved are changes too. A spoil timer that only counts down is not.

signals.name: BiomeChanged
signals.text: Fires when the character stands in another biome than at the last look. Looked at once a second.

signals.name: LevelUp
signals.text: Fires when the character's level went up. Looked at twice a second. Another character with a higher level is not a level up.

signals.name: XPGained
signals.text: Fires when the character earned experience: how much since the last look, and all it has now. Looked at twice a second.

signals.name: Respawned
signals.text: Fires when the character is alive after it was dead. Looked at four times a second.

signals.name: Spawned
signals.text: Fires when there is a character where there was none, or another one than before. It does not fire for the character that is there when you connect.

signals.name: Despawned
signals.text: Fires when the character that was there is gone. When another one takes its place at once, Despawned fires first and Spawned after it.

types.name: WaxModifier
types.title: WaxModifier
types.text: One effect that is on a character, as GetModifiers gives it. The game calls these modifiers: what food, drink, weather, wounds and gear put on a character.

props.name: Name
props.text: The modifier's row in the game's table D_ModifierStates, such as "Dirty_Water".
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].Name)

props.name: DisplayName
props.text: The name the game shows for it, such as "Tainted Water". The row name when the table gives none.
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].DisplayName)

props.name: Kind
props.text: The type the game's table gives it. nil when the table gives none Wax knows.
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].Kind)

props.name: Id
props.text: The number the game gave this one when it was put on. One put on later has a higher number.
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].Id)

props.name: Duration
props.text: How long it lasts in all, in seconds, as the game has it set. nil for one that lasts as long as its cause does, such as exposure to a storm.
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].Duration)

props.name: Remaining
props.text: How long it still lasts, in seconds. nil when Duration is.
props.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()
print(modifiers[1].Remaining)

types.name: WaxCharacterStats
types.title: WaxCharacterStats
types.text: What Wax adds to every character about its stats and its modifiers: every Instance whose class is IcarusCharacter or is built on it, a player's and a creature's. game.Me has the same for your own character. GetStat and the two regen fields ask the game for the one stat each time, so they answer for every stat the game has and are never out of date. Stats is the list the game keeps on the character for every player to see: the game puts some of its stats in that list and keeps the others out of it, and a character's list holds only those it has a value for. That list is read at most five times a second.
types.use: local character = game.Character

props.name: Stats
props.text: Every stat in the character's list, as name -> value: `character.Stats["MovementSpeed_+"]`. A new table each time. Putting names to the list costs more than one stat does, so do not read it every frame. The first read on a map also reads the names of all the game's stats, once. A stat the game keeps out of the list is not in it: ask GetStat for that one. nil when the character has no stats.

props.name: HealthRegen
props.text: The value of the game's stat HealthRegenPerMinute_+, read as GetStat reads it.

props.name: StaminaRegen
props.text: The value of the game's stat StaminaRegenPerMinute_+, read as GetStat reads it.

funcs.name: GetStat
funcs.text: The value of one stat, by its name in the game's table D_Stats: "MovementSpeed_+", "MaximumHealth_+", "WeightCapacity_+". Letter case does not matter. A name the game does not have raises an error that suggests the nearest ones. The game itself is asked, so this answers for every stat, also one the game keeps out of the character's list such as BaseMaximumHealth_+. The answer is 0 for a stat the character has no value for, and nil for a character with no stats.
funcs.use:
local character = game.Character
local result = character:GetStat(name)

funcs.name: GetModifiers
funcs.text: The modifiers that are on the character now, the one put on first at the front. An empty list when there are none. The tables are new each time. The character is asked once a frame, however often this is called in it.
funcs.use:
local character = game.Character
local modifiers = character:GetModifiers()

funcs.name: HasModifier
funcs.text: True when a modifier with this row name of D_ModifierStates is on the character now, such as "Berry". Letter case does not matter. A name the game does not have raises an error that suggests the nearest ones.
funcs.use:
local character = game.Character
local result = character:HasModifier(name)

funcs.name: AddModifier

params.name: seconds
params.text: How long it stays, above 0: a number, or a table such as { seconds = 60 }.

returns.name: id
returns.text: The number the game gave it, which GetModifiers lists as Id. nil when the game did not put it on.

funcs.text: Puts a modifier on the character. The modifier is named by its row of D_ModifierStates, such as "Health_Regen", in any letter case, and a name the game does not have raises an error that suggests the nearest ones. How long it stays has to be given: the game's table keeps no time of its own for a modifier. It is on at once, and GetModifiers and HasModifier say so in the same frame. It has been tried on a player's character. The game's table marks some modifiers as not for creatures.
funcs.use:
local character = game.Character
local id = character:AddModifier(name, seconds)

funcs.name: RemoveModifier

returns.name: count
returns.text: How many were taken off. 0 when none of that name was on.

funcs.text: Takes modifiers off the character at once. With a name, every modifier of that row. With a record that GetModifiers gave, the one with that Id.
funcs.use:
local character = game.Character
local count = character:RemoveModifier(modifier)

types.name: WaxTime
types.title: game.Time
types.text: The time of day in the prospect, game.Time. Each field asks the game when it is read. Every field is nil while you are not in a prospect. No field can be assigned: Set moves the clock.

props.name: Hour
props.text: The hour of the game's clock, from 0 to 23.

props.name: Minute
props.text: The minute within the hour, from 0 to 59.

props.name: Clock
props.text: The time as text, hours and minutes on a 24 hour clock: "7:05", "19:30".

props.name: Phase
props.text: The part of the day, by the hours of the game's table D_TimeOfDay: "Morning" from 6, "Day" from 10, "Afternoon" from 14, "Night" from 18 to 6. nil when the table gives none for the time.

props.name: IsNight
props.text: True while Phase is "Night".

props.name: Scale
props.text: The speed the game's clock is set to: 1 as the game sets it. The clock does not run evenly through the day at one Scale, and runs faster at night, so read Hour and do not work it out from seconds. The first read on a map looks the game's clock up, which costs more than the reads after it.

signals.name: HourChanged
signals.text: Fires when the hour is not what it was at the last look. Looked at twice a second, and only while a handler is connected. It does not fire for the hour that is found when you connect, nor for the first hour found on another map.
signals.use:
local time = game.Time
time.HourChanged:Connect(function(hour, previous)
    print(hour, previous)
end)

funcs.name: Set

params.name: hour
params.text: From 0 to 23.

params.name: minute
params.text: From 0 to 59. 0 when omitted.

returns.name: set
returns.text: True when the clock says that time afterwards.

funcs.text: Moves the game's clock forward to a time later today. The game's clock only goes forward within a day. It would count an earlier time as the next day, and Wax does not do that yet, so an earlier time raises an error that says what the clock shows. The minute the clock is already in changes nothing.
funcs.use:
local time = game.Time
local set = time:Set(hour, minute)

types.name: WaxWeatherEvent
types.title: WaxWeatherEvent
types.text: One weather event that is running somewhere on the map, as game.Weather.Active lists it.

props.name: Event
props.text: The event's row in the game's table D_WeatherEvents, such as "T2_Arctic_Snow".

props.name: Biome
props.text: The biome it is running in, as a row of D_Biomes such as "Arctic".

props.name: Since
props.text: When it began, in seconds on the clock that game.Prospect.Elapsed counts.

props.name: Tier
props.text: The event's tier in D_WeatherEvents, from 0 to 6.

types.name: WaxWeather
types.title: game.Weather
types.text: The weather, game.Weather. Current, Tier and IsStorm are about the weather on your own character, which the game tells every player. Active is the whole map, which only the host has.

props.name: Current
props.text: The weather event your character is in, as a row of D_WeatherEvents such as "T3_Conifer_Rain". nil in clear weather and while you have no character.

props.name: Tier
props.text: The tier of that event in D_WeatherEvents: 0 for the lightest, such as showers, up to 6 for the heaviest. nil in clear weather.

props.name: IsStorm
props.text: True while your character is in weather of tier 1 or more.

props.name: Active
props.text: Every weather event that is running on the map, one entry for each biome it runs in. It reads each of them, so do not read it every frame. nil when you are a client in someone else's game, and outside a prospect.

signals.name: Changed
signals.text: Fires when the weather on your character is another event than at the last look, with nil for clear weather. Looked at once a second, and only while a handler is connected. It does not fire for the weather that is found when you connect, nor for the first found on another map.
signals.use:

weather.Changed:Connect(function(current, previous)
    print(current, previous)
end)

types.name: WaxProspect
types.title: game.Prospect
types.text: The prospect you are in, game.Prospect. Each field asks the game when it is read. Every field is nil while you are not in a prospect.

props.name: Id
props.text: The game's own id for this prospect, a long text of letters and digits.

props.name: Name

props.name: Mission
props.text: The mission's row in D_FactionMissions, such as "OLY_Forest_Recon". nil when the prospect has none.

props.name: Difficulty
props.text: The prospect's difficulty.

props.name: Elapsed
props.text: How long the prospect has run, in seconds.

props.name: Duration
props.text: How long the prospect lasts in all, in seconds.

props.name: Remaining
props.text: Duration less Elapsed, and never below 0. nil when the game gives no Duration above 0.

props.name: IsOpenWorld
props.text: The game's own mark for an open world prospect.

props.name: IsOutpost
props.text: The game's own mark for an outpost.

props.name: Seed
props.text: The game's seed for this prospect.

types.name: WaxPlayer

props.name: PlayerName
props.text: The player's name. nil while the game has not said.

props.name: IsHost

props.name: Character

types.name: WaxItemFacts

types.text: What a kind of item is, from the game's own tables. The table is yours: changing it changes nothing in the game.

props.name: Description

props.use:
local items = game.Items
local itemFacts = items:Get(item)
print(itemFacts.Description)

props.name: Weight
props.text: What one of them weighs, in kilograms. nil for an item the game keeps no such facts about.
props.use:

local itemFacts = items:Get(item)
print(itemFacts.Weight)

props.name: MaxStack

local items = game.Items
local itemFacts = items:Get(item)

local items = game.Items

types.name: WaxItemStack
types.title: WaxItemStack
types.text: One stack in a slot of an inventory, as plain values. The table is yours: changing it changes nothing in the game.

props.name: Item
props.text: The item's name as the game spells it. The game's own files do not always use the same letter case, so compare two names without it, or ask Count, Has or Where.
props.use:

local itemStacks = backpack:List()
print(itemStacks[1].Item)

props.name: Count
props.text: How many are in the stack. 1 for an item the game keeps no stack number for.
props.use:
local backpack = game.Me.Backpack
local itemStacks = backpack:List()
print(itemStacks[1].Count)

props.name: Slot
props.text: The slot it is in, counted from 1. The game's own functions count from 0: their Location is Slot - 1.
props.use:
local backpack = game.Me.Backpack
local itemStacks = backpack:List()
print(itemStacks[1].Slot)

props.name: Durability
props.text: How much durability it has left. nil for an item the game keeps none for.
props.use:
local backpack = game.Me.Backpack
local itemStacks = backpack:List()
print(itemStacks[1].Durability)

props.name: Properties
props.text: Every number the game keeps for this stack, under the game's own name for it (EDynamicItemProperties): ItemableStack, Durability, GunCurrentMagSize, CurrentAmmoType, MillijoulesRemaining, TransmutableUnits, Fillable_StoredUnits, Fillable_Type, Decayable_CurrentSpoilTime and the others. One this version of Wax has no name for is under its number. nil when the game keeps none.

types.name: WaxInventory
types.title: WaxInventory
types.text: What Wax adds to every inventory: every Instance whose class is Inventory. A player's character has six of them, and other things that hold items have their own. Wax keeps a copy of an inventory that is asked about, so asking often costs little. It looks at the inventory again at most four times a second. When the weight or the number of slots is not what it was, every slot is read again. Otherwise a few slots are read in turn, so that all of them are read again within two seconds while you keep asking. An inventory that was not asked about for two seconds is read whole the next time. The game works a weight out a moment after the items change, so a new stack or a used-up one shows about a quarter of a second later, and what changes without the weight changing, such as durability or a stack moved to another slot, within two seconds. Refresh reads it all at once. Where the game itself tells Wax of a slot it changed, the copy follows at that moment and none of that waiting applies. That was seen for the inventories of a player's character on the host of a session. For a chest or a bench, and as a guest in someone else's game, it has not been tried, and there the looking above is what keeps the copy right. A field is nil, and a function raises an error that says so, when the game no longer keeps its inventories the way Wax reads them.

signals.name: ItemAdded
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?)>
signals.receives: item: string, amount: integer, stack: WaxItemStack?
signals.text: Fires when the inventory holds more of an item than a frame before: the item's name as the game spells it, how many more, and a stack it went onto. It is told by the game, for every slot the game says it changed, so it only fires where the game tells of an inventory: see above. A stack that moves to another slot of the same inventory within a frame is not added. Connecting reads the inventory whole once.

types.name: WaxCreatureMembers
types.title: WaxCreatureMembers
types.text: What Wax adds to a creature: every Instance whose class is IcarusNPCCharacter or IcarusPawn, or is built on one of them. Each field asks the game when it is read. A field is nil when the creature has no such value. Epic, Behaviour, Action, Target, Stance and IsFrozen are read from an IcarusNPCCharacter only. On the few creatures that are an IcarusPawn they are nil. Behaviour can be assigned, and SetLevel, Freeze, Unfreeze, Attack and Remove called. They are the game's own calls. In this version of Wax they are for wild animals that are an IcarusNPCCharacter. On a tamed animal and on an IcarusPawn each raises an error that says so, because the game's calls were only made on wild ones. No other field can be assigned. A creature that is an IcarusNPCCharacter is a character as well, so it also has what every character has: Health, Level, Alive, Heal, Kill, Teleport, Damaged, Died and the rest.
types.use: local creature = game.Creatures:GetNearest()

props.name: Kind
props.text: Its kind as the game's data names it, such as "Wolf". "Unknown" when the game's data does not say what it is.

props.name: Variant
props.text: The version of its kind, such as "Conifer_Wolf": a row of the table D_AISetup. nil when the game names none.

props.name: DisplayName
props.text: The name the game shows players for its kind, such as "Cave Worm".

props.name: Epic
props.text: The row of D_EpicCreatures that makes it a named boss or alpha, such as "AlphaWolf_Boss". nil for an ordinary creature.

props.name: Behaviour
props.text: The team the game has it on now, which decides whom it treats as an enemy: "Friendly" for the team FriendlyAll, "Tame" for Player (the players' own team), "HostileToPlayers" for EnemyPlayerOnly, "HostileToAll" for EnemyAll. On any other team it is "Default" while that is the team its variant starts on, and else the team's own name, a row of D_AIRelationships such as "DefaultLargeCarnivore". nil when the game names no team. It can be assigned: one of the five words, where "Default" puts it back on the team its variant starts on, or a team's own name. A name that is neither raises an error that suggests the nearest. The game goes by the new team from the next time the animal notices somebody, not at once: a wolf that had a player in view attacked two seconds after "HostileToPlayers", a wolf that was walking away did nothing in five, and an animal that is attacking goes on attacking after "Friendly".

props.name: Action
props.text: What it is doing now, as the game's class for that action is called: "Wander", "FindFood", "EmergeFromRetreat". nil while the game names none for it.

props.name: Target
props.text: The actor it is after right now, such as a player's character or another creature. nil while it is after nothing.

props.name: Stance
props.text: How it holds itself.

props.name: IsJuvenile
props.text: True for a young animal: one that a taming rule of the game, a row of D_Tames, names as the young of its kind. nil when the game's tables cannot be read.

props.name: IsTamed
props.text: True for an animal that has been tamed: a mount, a pet or livestock. The game makes these from classes built on IcarusMountCharacter, and that is what is looked at. A speeder bike counts as one, because the game builds it the same way.

props.name: CanBeTamed
props.text: True when a taming rule of the game names its variant, as the young animal or as the grown one, and it is not tamed already. It says what the game's data has, not whether a taming would work right now. nil when the game's tables cannot be read.

props.name: IsFrozen
props.text: True while the creature is held frozen, by Freeze or by the game itself. nil on a creature whose class has no such flag.

props.name: HasModel
props.text: True while the creature wears a model that SetModel gave it.

funcs.name: SetModel

returns.name: worn
returns.text: Always true.

funcs.text: Gives the creature another body: a skeletal mesh of the game or of your mod's own content, with its materials. It goes on moving as before, because the new body is on the same skeleton: a mesh on another skeleton raises an error that names both. The game writes a mount's own skin again now and then, so Wax looks once a second and puts the model back. When your mod unloads, or on ResetModel, the creature has its own body again. It works for the host and for a client alike, and each player only sees it in their own game.
funcs.use:
local creature = game.Creatures:GetNearest()
local worn = creature:SetModel(model)

funcs.name: ResetModel

returns.name: changed
returns.text: False when it wore no model.

funcs.text: Gives the creature the body it had before SetModel.

local changed = creature:ResetModel()

returns.name: why

funcs.text: Makes a mount attack, as the game does when its rider attacks: it plays the mount's own attack, takes the stamina that costs, and hits what stands in front of it at the strike. The game keeps this for mounts with the talent for it. Strike asks for no talent.

funcs.name: Unfreeze

returns.name: freed
returns.text: True when it was frozen and is free now. False when it was not frozen.

funcs.text: Lets a frozen creature go again. A deer walked on within half a second.
funcs.use:

local freed = creature:Unfreeze()

funcs.name: Attack

params.name: target
params.text: The player's character to go for, or game.Me.

returns.name: angry
returns.text: True when its aggression is raised afterwards.

funcs.text: Makes the creature angry at a player's character: the game raises its aggression to the most and tells it where the target is. A wolf had the character as its Target within a second or two and ran at it. It is for the animals the game gives aggression, the hunters. For one that has none, such as a deer or a rabbit, it raises an error that says so, and so it does for a target that is not a player's character. Nothing in Wax calls an attack off again. Remove takes the animal away.
funcs.use:

local angry = creature:Attack(target)

funcs.name: Remove

returns.name: asked
returns.text: Always true.

funcs.text: Takes the creature out of the world, alive or dead, with nothing left behind. The game does it a moment later, not in the same frame: IsValid() says when it is gone. The game replaces a dead creature by a corpse a few seconds after its death, one to three seconds when it was timed. The corpse is no creature: it is not in game.Creatures, and Remove raises an error on the creature it was, which is gone by then. A dead creature that was removed before that left no corpse.
funcs.use:
local creature = game.Creatures:GetNearest()
local asked = creature:Remove()

types.name: WaxDataTable
types.title: WaxDataTable
types.text: One of the game's data tables, such as ProcessorRecipes (every recipe) or Itemable (every item's name, icon and weight). A field path is a field's name, with a dot for each step into a struct or an array: "RequiredMillijoules", "Requirement.RowName", "Inputs.Element.RowName". Naming a struct or an array of structs asks for everything inside it. A wrong path raises an error that suggests the right one. Rows are read once and kept. A row is one table for as long as it is kept, and asking for more fields later adds them to that same table. Row names and field names are matched without regard to letter case. The keys of a row are spelled as the game spells them. Enum fields are read only when their own path is named, and they read as numbers. A map field is read only when its own path is named ("ArmourStats", "Creatures.WorldStatInjection"), and it is read whole: a path cannot go on into a map. It is a table from each key to its value. A key is a string or a number: a name, a string, the number of an enum, a whole number or a float, an asset's path, the row name of a row handle, and the one name inside a row enum or a tag, so a stat map reads `{ ["BaseMaximumHealth_+"] = 100 }`. An entry whose key is a reference to no asset is left out. A value is what a field of that kind is anywhere in a row: a number, true or false, a string, a struct as a table (a row handle among them, as its two names) without the enums, maps and curves inside it, an asset's path, or the numbers of a curve. A value that refers to nothing is false, so its key is still there. A map is refused when its keys are references to live objects, or structs other than a row handle and a struct with a single name or number in it, and when its values are lists, maps, sets or live objects other than curves. What a map holds is learned from the first entry read, so the error that says which of these it is comes when a row that has an entry in that map is read, and at once from then on. A map with more than 4,096 entries is not read: its row is nil and the log says why. A field that refers to a CurveFloat is read only when its own path is named, as a WaxDataCurve, or nil when it refers to nothing. A curve that several rows refer to is asked of the game once, and each row gets its own copy of the numbers. A field that refers to any other live object, such as a texture, raises an error when a row where it is set is read. Sets, delegates, doubles, weak references and lists of live objects are never read. Naming one raises an error that says what it is.
types.use: local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)

props.name: Name

props.text: The name of the struct every row of the table is, such as "ProcessorRecipe".

funcs.text: One row, or nil when the table has no row of this name or the row could not be read. With `fields` only those are read. Without it the row holds everything that is read without being named, which leaves out enums, maps and curves. To read a map or a curve, name it: `game.Data:Table("AIGrowth"):Row("Deer", { "Base", "Health" })`. A struct or a list that was read with a map or a curve inside it is refused by Set until that key is taken out again.

local dataRow = dataTable:Row(name, fields)

funcs.name: Load
funcs.text: Reads many rows without holding the game up, and returns them by name. It only works inside a task. The task pauses whenever it has used its budget for the frame, and goes on in the next one. Rows that already hold the fields are not read again, so a second Load costs nothing and a Load that was stopped goes on where it left off.

local rows = dataTable:Load(options)

local dataFields = dataTable:Fields(path)

funcs.name: Meta
funcs.text: The table's meta table, or nil when it has none. Its rows have the same names and say which expansion a row belongs to (RequiredFeatureLevel) and whether the game has retired it (bIsDeprecated). A meta table can be read, not changed.

local result = dataTable:Meta()

funcs.name: Stamp
funcs.text: The table's row count and address as text, such as "2215:0x1F3A2B40". It is checked against the game each time. Once a mod has changed the table, a third part counts what was written to it: "2215:0x1F3A2B40:7". The count only goes up. Keep the stamp beside anything you worked out from the table: a different stamp means the table is not what you read.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
local result = dataTable:Stamp()

funcs.name: Set
funcs.text: Gives one field of a row a new value in the game. It is written before Set returns, so whatever the game reads from the row next is the new value. `field` is a whole field of the row, such as "Inputs", not a path into one. The value is whole: a struct with each of its fields, a list with each of its entries, as Change hands it to its function. Row gives the same, except that it leaves an enum inside a struct out until that enum's own path is named (`Row(name, { "SessionRequirement.DataTableName" })`). Set needs it and raises "SessionRequirement lacks DataTableName" without it. Two things may be left out of a struct: a typed row handle's DataTableName, which is filled in from the kind of handle, and text and references to assets, which stay as they are. A typed row handle only takes its own table: an ItemsStaticRowHandle names a row of ItemsStatic and nothing else, apart from the table and row the field holds already. A table name is taken with or without "D_", in any letter case, and written as the game lists it. An enum takes its number. Once Wax has read a value of that field in this session (for a list: from a row where the list has an entry), the number has to be one the enum has or the one the field holds, and the enum's name as the game spells it is taken too. Until then a name raises an error that asks for the number. Everything is checked before anything is written: the row, the field, the kind of every value, and that a row handle or a row enum names a row its table has (a row the field already names may stay, as some of the game's own rows name rows that are not there). What is wrong raises an error that names the place, such as "Inputs[2] lacks Count". After the write the field is read again. If the game did not take the value, the old one is put back and an error says what differed. The change belongs to the mod that makes it and is put back when the mod unloads. A mod that makes the same change again in the frame it reloads, or within 2 seconds of it, writes nothing. A change it no longer makes is put back when those 2 seconds are over. After a reload the row may still hold the mod's own earlier value, so a new value worked out from what the row holds belongs in Change. When two mods set one field, the mod that loads later is used, and Conflicts lists the field. With a table of fields in place of the field name, every value is checked before any is written. Two keys that mean the same field, such as Count and count, are an error. This version does not change text, references to assets, maps, sets, doubles or references to live objects. A list whose entries only the game can make (they hold one of those, a row enum or a multi row handle) keeps its length: its entries can be changed where they are, not added or removed. A kind of change that this version has switched off raises an error that says so. That can be a list that would get longer or shorter while it has more than 4 entries, while it is inside another value, or while its entries are strings or can hold strings or lists of their own. It can also be a row handle pointed at another table than the one it names now.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
dataTable:Set(row, field, value)

funcs.name: Change
funcs.text: Changes one field of a row from the value it has. `fn` gets a copy of the whole value, enums included as numbers, and returns the new one. For a struct or a list it may change the copy and return nothing. The result is checked and written as Set does it. Wax keeps the function and runs it again when a mod that loads earlier changes the field or unloads, so it should depend on nothing but the value it is given. It has to return at once: a function that waits (`task.wait`, `Signal:Wait`, `Table:Load`) is an error. Changes of two mods to one field both hold: each builds on the other's, in the order the mods load. Change adds to what this mod changed in the field before. Set starts over.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
dataTable:Change(row, field, function(value) end)

funcs.name: Add

params.name: values
params.text: Fields of the new row, each as Set takes it.

funcs.text: Adds a row: a copy of the row `options.like` names, as that row is now, with `values` written over it as Set would. Returns the row's name. The name is letters, digits and underscores and begins with the mod's id and an underscore, such as "MyMod_Quick_Axe". A character of the id that is none of those counts as an underscore. The game's own index of the table is renewed, so the game knows the row at once. The row belongs to the mod that added it, and Add again for the same row uses the row that is there. When the mod unloads, what it wrote into the row is put back and the row stays in the table, because a row is not taken out while the game runs. A recipe is switched off then: bForceDisableRecipe is set and it is on no bench, which takes it off the game's lists. The game still makes it when something asks for it by name. A row of another table is left as it is. A row that could not be switched off like that in this version is refused as the row to start from, with an error that says why. A row of the game is never replaced or removed. While adding rows is switched off in a version of Wax, Add raises an error that says so.
funcs.use:
local dataTable = game.Data:Table(name)
local result = dataTable:Add(name, values, options)

returns.text: How many changes were taken back.

funcs.text: Takes this mod's changes back: of one field, of one row when no field is given, of the whole table when no row is given. A row this mod added is switched off as when the mod unloads. What other mods changed stays. If the game does not take a field back, Reset raises an error and that change stands as before, so Reset can be called again.

local count = dataTable:Reset(row, field)

local dataConflicts = dataTable:Conflicts()

types.name: WaxData
types.title: game.Data
types.text: The game's data tables as plain Lua values: recipes, items, creatures, talents and the rest. Nothing is read until you ask, and what was read is kept, so asking twice costs nothing. Text is kept in the language the game was showing when it was read. After the player changes the language it shows in the new one only after Flush, or when the game starts again.

signals.name: Changed
signals.text: Fires when what was read from a table no longer holds: the game made the table again, or rows of it were written for a mod (then at the end of that frame, once for the table). While many fields are put back over several frames it fires at most four times a second, and once when the put-back is done. `name` is the table's name, or nil when everything was dropped. Flush fires it too, with no name.

signals.name: Patched
signals.type: WaxSignal<fun(table: string, row: string, field: string?)>
signals.receives: table: string, row: string, field: string?
signals.text: Fires for each field of a row that was written, by a mod's change, by a Reset or because a mod unloaded: at the end of that frame, or together with Changed while many fields are put back over several frames. `field` is nil when the row itself was added, switched off or taken out.

funcs.text: The row a row handle points at, and the table it is in. Nil when the handle points at nothing or at a row the game does not have. A handle whose DataTableName was not read as a name raises an error. Read such a row with Table and Row.

funcs.name: Flush
funcs.text: Forgets everything that was read, so the next read asks the game again. Use it after the player changes the game's language. Rows handed out before stay as they are and are no longer filled in. Changed fires at the end of the frame, so every mod that keeps something worked out from rows can work it out again. What mods changed in the tables stays changed.

types.title: WaxDataRow
types.text: One row of a data table as plain Lua values, shaped like the game's own data files with every default filled in. `Name` is the row's name. A struct is a table and an array is a list. A name, a string and a text are Lua strings. A reference to an asset is its path, or nil when it points at nothing (false inside a list or a map). A map is a table from each key to its value, and a reference to a curve is a WaxDataCurve. Both are only there when their own path was named. A row is shared by everyone who reads it, so never change one. To change what the game holds, use Set, Change or Add.

types.name: WaxRecipe
types.title: WaxRecipe
types.text: One crafting recipe: a row of D_ProcessorRecipes. `game.Recipes:Get("Stone_Axe")` gives one. Reading a field reads the game's table, so it is always what the table holds now. The lists it gives are yours to change: that changes nothing in the game. One exception keeps a mod steady while it is being reloaded: what the mod itself wrote before the reload is left out, so `if recipe.Work > 2000 then recipe:SetWork(2000) end` does the same thing each time. Every function that changes the recipe returns the recipe, so changes can follow one another: `game.Recipes:Get("Stone_Axe"):SetInputs({ Stone = 1 }):SetSeconds(1)`. A change is written before the function returns. It belongs to the mod that makes it and is put back when the mod unloads, as every change of game.Data is. What two mods do to one recipe is worked out in the order the mods load. SetInput, RemoveInput, the Scale functions, AddBench, RemoveBench and the output functions build on what an earlier mod did. SetInputs, SetBenches, MoveTo, SetWork, SetSeconds, SetRequirement, Hide and Show replace it, and `game.Data:Conflicts()` lists a field where that hides another mod's different value. What a change does to something that is being made or waiting in a queue, as it was seen on the host: a new time counts from the next moment, so what is half done by the old time may be nearly done, or done, by the new one. What is taken and what comes out is read from the recipe when the making ends, as the recipe is then. Nothing is taken before that. As soon as the player cannot pay what the recipe takes, the making is dropped without a message, and nothing is lost. So change recipes when the mod loads if a player should never see one change while it is being made. Names of items, benches, recipes and nodes are matched without regard to letter case. A name the game does not have raises an error that suggests the nearest ones. This version of Wax cannot make every list of a recipe longer or shorter. The outputs keep their number: each can become another item and another count. The resources keep their number too. The items, the tags and the benches of a recipe can be added to and taken from while the list has 4 entries or fewer, before and after. A change that is refused raises an error that says so, and changes nothing.
types.use: local recipe = game.Recipes:Get(name)

funcs.name: GetSeconds
funcs.text: How long making the recipe once takes at a bench, in seconds, before talents and upgrades. Without a bench it is the time at the recipe's own benches. When those work at different speeds, or Wax does not know how fast one works, it raises an error that says so.

funcs.name: SetInputs
funcs.text: Sets the items the recipe takes: `recipe:SetInputs({ Wood = 2, Fiber = 4 })`. Written like that they are put in the order of their names. A list keeps the order it is given in: `{ { "Wood", 2 }, { "Fiber", 4 } }`, or `{ { Item = "Wood", Count = 2 } }`. What the recipe takes by tag and its resources stay as they are. A count is a whole number of 1 or more. An empty table is refused when the recipe would then take nothing at all.

local result = recipe:SetInputs(inputs)

funcs.name: SetInput

params.name: count
params.text: A whole number of 1 or more.

funcs.text: Sets how many of one thing the recipe takes, and adds it when the recipe does not take it yet: `recipe:SetInput("Wood", 2)`. The name is an item, a tag or a resource. A resource can only be changed where the recipe already takes it.

local result = recipe:SetInput(name, count)

funcs.name: RemoveInput
funcs.text: Takes one item or tag out of what the recipe takes. params.name: factor
params.text: A number above 0.

params.name: count

funcs.name: SetWork

params.name: millijoules
params.text: A whole number of 1 or more.

funcs.name: SetSeconds

params.name: seconds
params.text: A number above 0.

funcs.name: ScaleTime

params.name: factor

funcs.name: Hide
funcs.text: Takes the recipe off the lists players choose from. The crafting tab and the game's own list of a bench's recipes were seen to drop it. types.name: WaxRecipes
types.title: game.Recipes
types.text: The game's crafting recipes: finding them and changing them. `game.Recipes:Get("Stone_Axe"):SetInputs({ Stone = 1 })` makes a stone axe cost one stone, and `game.Recipes:At("Fabricator"):ScaleTime(0.5)` makes everything the Fabricator makes twice as fast. Every change goes through game.Data, so it is checked first, put back when the mod unloads, and listed by `game.Data:Changes()`.

funcs.name: Get
funcs.text: One recipe by its name, at once: nothing of the recipe is read until a field is asked for. A name the game does not have raises an error that suggests the nearest ones, so ask Has first when the name may be wrong. The recipe for an item often has the item's name, but not always, and some items have several recipes: Making finds them all.
funcs.use: local recipe = game.Recipes:Get(name)

funcs.name: Has
funcs.text: True when the game has a recipe of this name.
funcs.use: local result = game.Recipes:Has(name)

funcs.name: All
funcs.text: Every recipe the game has. Nothing is read for it.
funcs.use: local recipeList = game.Recipes:All()

funcs.name: At
funcs.text: The recipes a bench lists: `game.Recipes:At("Fabricator")`, `game.Recipes:At("Hand")`. A bench is named by the item that is the bench, by its recipe set, or "Hand". A hidden recipe is on no bench's list, and what a player has researched makes no difference to the list. In a prospect the game itself is asked, which took 1 to 3 milliseconds when it was measured. Its answer for a bench is kept until a recipe is written, so asking again costs under a millisecond. Anywhere else, and when the game does not answer, the recipe table is read instead, as Using does it.
funcs.use: local recipeList = game.Recipes:At(bench)

funcs.name: Making
funcs.text: The recipes that give an item: `game.Recipes:Making("Rope")`. The name is an item, or a template. It reads what every recipe gives and every template's item. Inside a task that pauses when it has used a millisecond of a frame. Anywhere else it is read at once, which the first time is a frame the player can notice. What was read is kept, and looking through it still took 8 milliseconds when it was measured, so search when the mod loads, not in every frame.
funcs.use: local recipeList = game.Recipes:Making(item)

funcs.name: Using
funcs.text: The recipes that take an item, a tag or a resource: `game.Recipes:Using("Fiber")`. It reads what every recipe takes. Inside a task that pauses when it has used a millisecond of a frame. Anywhere else it is read at once, which the first time is a frame the player can notice. What was read is kept, and looking through it still took 10 milliseconds when it was measured, so search when the mod loads, not in every frame.
funcs.use: local recipeList = game.Recipes:Using(name)

funcs.name: Find
funcs.text: The recipes `fn` returns true for: `game.Recipes:Find(function(recipe) return recipe.Work > 10000 end)`. It asks about every recipe, and each field `fn` reads is read from the game the first time. Inside a task it pauses when it has used a millisecond of a frame.
funcs.use: local recipeList = game.Recipes:Find(function(recipe) end)

funcs.name: Add
funcs.text: Adds a recipe: a copy of the recipe `options.like` names, changed by the other options. `game.Recipes:Add("MyMod_Quick_Axe", { like = "Stone_Axe", inputs = { Stone = 1 }, seconds = 1 })`. The name begins with the mod's id and an underscore. It is switched off in this version of Wax and raises an error that says so: adding a row to the game's tables while the game runs has not been seen working yet.
funcs.use: local recipe = game.Recipes:Add(name, options)
